#### Disclaimer

:::{.disclaimer_box}
::::{.disclaimer_box_header}
Disclaimer
::::
::::{.inner_block}
The purpose of the [Open Case Studies](https://opencasestudies.github.io){target="_blank"} project is **to demonstrate the use of various data science methods, tools, and software in the context of messy, real-world data**. A given case study does not cover all aspects of the research process, is not claiming to be the most appropriate way to analyze a given data set, and should not be used in the context of making policy or clinical decisions without external consultation from scientific experts or medical care professionals. In addition, due to size constraints, datasets used within a case study may be a subset of the original/full dataset.
::::
:::

## How to Use This Case Study 
***

The purpose of this collection of case studies is to provide an educational resource of experiential guides to demonstrate how to work through the full process of a specific type of data analysis (or use of a data science best practice). 

This case study is modular, which means that you can work through the full case study as written, or choose sections that focus on the desired skills that you would like to learn and practice. The [learning objective map](add link to objective map here!) can be used to determine which sections of the case study correspond with each learning objective. The [continued learning section](add link to continued learning section) at the end of the case study will provide next steps and additional tasks to practice the skills learned in the case study.

As you work through the case study, you will come across the following components:

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Instructions

Instructions will appear in yellow tabs throughout the case study.
:::

<details><summary>Click-to-expand boxes will hold additional information</summary>

When clicked on, these boxes will expand to provide additional information on specific topics.

</details>

:::{.definition_box}
::::{.definition_box_header}
Definition
::::
::::{.inner_block}
Definition boxes will define key terms for the case study. Other terms that may be unfamiliar will be included in the glossary. These terms will appear in the case study highlighted with purple text, and can be clicked on to see the definition, such as {{< glossary "Term 1" >}}.
::::
:::

:::{.think_question}
::::{.think_question_header}
Question opportunity
::::
::::{.inner_block}
Question opportunities will give you the chance to test your comprehension.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Some questions will have answers that can be clicked-to-expand to evaluate your own responses.
</details>
::::
:::

:::{.reproducibility_box}
::::{.reproducibility_box_header}
Reproducibility considerations
::::
::::{.inner_block}
Reproducibility boxes will highlight specific reproducibility guidelines or best practices as they come up within the case study.
::::
:::

:::{.decision-point}

Decision point boxes can be expanded to describe considerations around a decision that must be made in a specific step of the case study. The full set of decision points will be summarized in the [decision point map](link to decision point map).

:::

:::{.troubleshooting}

Troubleshooting boxes can be expanded to describe a common problem that may occur at a specific step of the case study, as well as ways to troubleshoot the problem.

:::

:::{.ai_box}
::::{.ai_box_header}
AI use considerations
::::
::::{.inner_block}

AI use consideration boxes will note when AI can be used for a specific task (or cases in which AI should only be used with caution).

<u>Context:</u>

Context for the specific AI use will be provided here.

<u>Suggested Prompt:</u>

```{ .default .code-overflow-wrap }
Suggested prompts to be copied and pasted will be provided here. 
```

<u>Validation:</u>
Additional guidance to check or validate the AI response will be provided here. 

::::
:::
